newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin aims to bump G7 up to "G8" in Denver.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin aims to bump G7 up to "G8" in Denver.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, keeping up a brisk pace in foreign policy, aims to see Russia become a member of a new "Group of Eight" countries at a G7 summit in the United States next month, his spokesman said on Friday.
"After this meeting the Group of Seven is transformed into G8," said Kremlin spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky, quoted by Russia's Interfax news agency.
The summit will take place in Denver from June 20-22 and Yeltsin agreed with U.S. President Bill Clinton in March that it would be called the "Summit of the Eight".

Their deal gave Russia a bigger role while stopping short of full membership for Moscow. But earlier this month Japan dropped its opposition to letting Russia join the grouping of leading industrialised nations as a formal member.
Japan's reluctance to have Russia as a formal member stemmed from a territorial dispute over four islands of Japan's northernmost main island seized by the Soviet Union at the end of World War Two.

The dispute remains unresolved but frosty relations between Moscow and Tokyo are improving. Last week Yeltsin thanked visiting Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda for Tokyo's backing Moscow's bid to join the G7.

Yeltsin, fresh from his show-stealing performance in Paris on Tuesday where he signed a new partnership for security in Europe with NATO, has a "rather intense" schedule in coming weeks, Interfax quoted Yastrzhembsky as saying.

He is poised for a foreign policy breakthough in Russia's troubled relations with neighbouring Ukraine on Saturday when he is scheduled to sign a friendship and cooperation treaty with Ukrainian counterpart Leonid Kuchma.
The treaty and Yeltsin's visit to Ukraine has been called off several times in bickering over debts and the division of the Soviet Black Sea Fleet.
Earlier, Yastrzhembsky said that Yeltsin viewed his Kiev visit as even more important than this week's summit with leaders of the western defence alliance.
"The closer the ties between Russia and Ukraine, the fewer the headaches in its (Russia's) relations with NATO," Interfax quoted him as saying.
Yastrzhembsky said Yeltsin would meet Russia's regional leaders on June 4 and visit St Petersburg on June 6 to check on the condition of historical monuments in Russia's second city.
He added Yeltsin would meet the leaders of Belarus, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan -- all members of a troubled customs union -- on June 26.
